when: Mid-March, when the first rains settle
why: The soil pH fits maize, and the season ends before the second rains. The mean temperature is below the crop's optimum range, so this is a cautious pick.
reasons: Site pH 6.12 is inside the maize range of 5.5 to 7.0.
A 110-day maize season from mid-March ends in early July, before the second rains.
The site mean of 25.4 C is below the 30 to 34 C optimum, so temperature is not a pass.
card_en: Plant maize at the start of the first rains, usually mid-March. The soil pH fits and a 110-day season ends in early July, before the second rains. The mean temperature is below the crop's optimum range, so treat this as a cautious choice. Common bean is the supported alternative.
season_assumption: This advice assumes the first rains season: the timing uses the median first-rains onset, and the window closes after 110 growing days.
card_lg: Simba kasooli mu ntandikwa ya nkuba ezisooka. Ettaka lino lya bulungi. Ebbugumu lya wansi ku kigero kya kasooli, kale kino kya kulowooza. Ebijanjaalo bye birala ebisobola okusimbibwa.
